phases.name: Audit and validate existing Ca/Ce computation

steps.name: Audit Ca scoring bands and median semantics
steps.criteria: Tests confirm that: (1) afferent_coupling returns score=100 when import_graph is empty, (2) a single hub file with 20 dependents scores 100 because median Ca across all files is 0, (3) a fully-connected 10-file graph where every file has Ca=9 scores <=50, (4) the description string contains 'median:', 'mean:', and 'max:'. All four assertions already pass without code change; any failing assertion reveals a computation bug that must be fixed before proceeding.

steps.name: Audit Ce scoring bands and median semantics
steps.criteria: Tests confirm that: (1) efferent_coupling returns score=100 when import_graph is empty, (2) a single heavy importer (25 deps) among 36 files scores 100 because median Ce is 0, (3) 10 files each with Ce=15 scores 25, (4) the description string contains 'median:', 'mean:', and 'max:'. All four assertions already pass without code change; any failing assertion reveals a computation bug that must be fixed.

phases.name: Data model: per-file coupling metrics in AnalysisReport

steps.name: Add FileCouplingMetrics struct and per_file_coupling field to AnalysisReport
steps.criteria: A new public struct FileCouplingMetrics is added to src/scorer/types.rs with fields: path: String, ca: usize, ce: usize, instability: f64. The AnalysisReport struct gains a new field per_file_coupling: Vec<FileCouplingMetrics>. The field is serialized by serde (appears in JSON output). build_report() populates it by calling a new builder function. A test in src/scorer.rs asserts that build_report() with an empty snapshot produces an empty per_file_coupling vec. No abstractness field is added at this stage (no abstract/concrete classification data available in RepoSnapshot).

steps.name: Implement build_per_file_coupling() builder function
steps.criteria: A pure function build_per_file_coupling(snapshot: &RepoSnapshot) -> Vec<FileCouplingMetrics> is added to src/scorer/builders.rs. For each file in snapshot.files: ca = count of files in import_graph whose target list contains this file's path; ce = import_graph.get(&file.path).map(|v| v.len()).unwrap_or(0); instability = if ca + ce == 0 { 0.0 } else { ce as f64 / (ca + ce) as f64 }. The result is sorted descending by instability, then by path as a tiebreaker. Tests cover: (1) file with no imports and no dependents has ca=0, ce=0, instability=0.0; (2) file imported by 3 others and importing 1 has ca=3, ce=1, instability=0.25; (3) file with ce=5 and ca=0 has instability=1.0 (maximally unstable); (4) file with ca=5 and ce=0 has instability=0.0 (maximally stable). Function signature follows (snapshot -> value) pattern with no mutation of inputs.

phases.name: HTML renderer: instability panel in Coupling tab

steps.name: Add instability summary section to buildCouplingTab()
steps.criteria: In src/renderer/html/js_coupling.rs, buildCouplingTab() is extended to render a second panel below the temporal coupling table. The panel reads R.per_file_coupling (an array of {path, ca, ce, instability} objects). If the array is absent or empty, the panel displays 'No static import data available.' Otherwise it renders a table with columns: File, Ca (afferent), Ce (efferent), Instability. Each instability value is coloured: <=0.3 green (var(--c-good)), <=0.7 amber (var(--c-warn)), >0.7 red (var(--c-danger)). An inline bar proportional to instability is shown beside the value. The table is capped at 50 rows. A panel header explains: 'Instability = Ce / (Ca + Ce). 0 = maximally stable (depended upon, changes carefully). 1 = maximally unstable (depends on others, safe to change freely).' No innerHTML is used; all DOM nodes created via el() and txt() helpers.

steps.name: Add column tooltips and sort-by-instability default to instability table
steps.criteria: The instability table in buildCouplingTab() uses thWithTip() for column headers with the following tooltip text: Ca — 'Afferent coupling: number of files that import this file. High Ca = many dependents, risky to change.'; Ce — 'Efferent coupling: number of files this file imports. High Ce = many dependencies.'; Instability — 'Ce / (Ca + Ce). 0 = stable (depended upon). 1 = unstable (depends on others).'. Rows are sorted by instability descending before rendering (pure sort on R.per_file_coupling.slice(), no mutation of original array). A test asserts the rendered HTML string contains the tooltip text for each column header.

phases.name: CLI and JSON output: surface instability in analyze output

steps.name: JSON output includes per_file_coupling array automatically
steps.criteria: Because AnalysisReport is serialized via serde_json::to_value in src/renderer/json.rs, the per_file_coupling field added in step 02-01 appears in JSON output with no renderer changes. A test in src/renderer/json.rs asserts that render(&report_with_one_coupling_entry, false, None) produces JSON where parsed["per_file_coupling"] is an array of length 1 containing an object with keys 'path', 'ca', 'ce', 'instability'. A second test asserts that a report with an empty per_file_coupling produces parsed["per_file_coupling"] as an empty array (not absent).

steps.name: CLI analyze output shows top unstable files in Coupling category
steps.criteria: In the CLI renderer (src/renderer/cli.rs or equivalent), after the existing Coupling category score block, print a compact 'Top unstable files' section showing up to 5 files from per_file_coupling sorted by instability descending. Each line format: '  {instability:.2}  {path}  (Ca={ca}, Ce={ce})'. The section is skipped entirely when per_file_coupling is empty. A unit test asserts that rendering a report with three coupling entries prints lines containing the instability values in descending order and the file paths. A second test asserts that rendering a report with empty per_file_coupling produces no 'unstable' text in the output.
